subject: Temporary retention exception for migration — negotiation and rollback trigger
messages:
From: Legal Ops (Medicore) <legalops@medicore.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: DPO - Medicore <dpo@medicore.com>, infra@medicore.com
Date: 2026-10-12T08:22:00+01:00
Subject: Temporary retention exception for migration - request & subprocessor details

Hi Hannah,

We are planning a cross-region data migration for a subset of our production project (project id: MED-PROJ-21). The infra team is requesting a temporary retention window extension for backups and logs to support rollback testing and data integrity checks.

What we need from Redwood:
- A formal temporary retention exception of up to 45 days for backups associated with MED-PROJ-21 (we understand normal retention is 14 days).
- A documented rollback trigger definition (conditions that will cause us to restore from backups).
- An updated subprocessors list for the affected backup/restore flow and confirmation there are no additional unidentified subprocessors.
- Evidence that the backups will be purged immediately after the agreed window unless a rollback is triggered.

Attached: migration_plan_v2.pdf, subprocessor_matrix.csv (the infra team exported their current map).

We'd like to get this signed as an addendum to the DPA (if required) before the migration window starts: target week of 26 Oct. Please confirm what you need from our side to move quickly.

Thanks,
Sofia Ruiz
Legal Ops — Medicore Health
[Attachment: migration_plan_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: subprocessor_matrix.csv (text/csv, 45KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Legal Ops (Medicore) <legalops@medicore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T11:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention exception for migration - request & subprocessor details

Sofia — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Looping our legal (Kimberly), privacy (Karthik), and ops (Laura) so we can align quickly. A couple of quick clarifying questions from our side:

1) Can you confirm whether the requested retention applies only to encrypted incremental backups and ephemeral KV logs, or also to full nightly snapshots?
2) Are the backups encrypted with your KMS or via Redwood-managed keys? If cross-border keys are involved we will need explicit DPA language.

We will put a short proposed timeline and rollback-trigger definition together and send an addendum draft for signature (DocuSign) by EOD Tuesday 20 Oct.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: (none)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T09:16:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention exception for migration - request & subprocessor details

Hannah / team — I reviewed Medicore's subprocessor_matrix.csv. The file looks consistent with our records but two notes:

- We must require an explicit DPA addendum that:
  * limits the retention extension to a named project (MED-PROJ-21) and expiration date;
  * mandates immediate purge unless rollback is executed;
  * requires Medicore to sign off on any request to keep backups longer than the agreed window.

- For the DocuSign workflow, I'll prepare an addendum template that attaches the migration_plan_v2.pdf as exhibit A and includes the rollback trigger passage. Proposed default window: 30 days. If Medicore insists on 45 days they must provide a business justification and a procurement sign-off.

I'll draft the addendum and post the DocuSign link by Monday 19 Oct. Karthik, please confirm privacy guardrails below.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood
[Attachment: redwood_dpa_addendum_template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 75KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T14:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention exception for migration - request & subprocessor details

Quick privacy notes:
- From a GDPR standpoint, a limited, documented retention extension is acceptable provided Medicore documents the legal basis and scope in writing (processing purpose: migration/rollback testing). We should require Medicore to provide the written purpose and retain it as evidence.
- I prefer 30 days for the extension with the ability to extend to 45 days only via a documented escalation (email from Medicore legal + procurement approval).
- Require audit logging for access to extended backups: token-level access logs retained for 1 year (to support any post-rollback investigation).
- Cross-border transfer: if any backups are routed through non-EEA infrastructure, add a transfer clause referencing SCCs or an inline DPA transfer mechanism.

Operationally, Laura — can we support staggered purge (e.g., snapshot TTLs with automatic purge tasks) and a single-panel rollback trigger (ops playbook) that Medicore can call out of band? If yes, ensure we capture the RTO/RPO tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy — Redwood

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Legal Ops (Medicore) <legalops@medicore.com>, DPO - Medicore <dpo@medicore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:15:00+01:00
Subject: Proposed temporary-retention addendum and rollback trigger — MED-PROJ-21 (draft)

Sofia — attached is our proposed addendum (redwood_temp-retention-proposal_20261020.pdf) and a short ops runbook for the rollback trigger. Summary of the proposal below: 

- Retention window: 30 days starting on the date of the migration. Extension to 45 days allowed only with written Medicore procurement approval and formal business justification.
- Scope: incremental encrypted backups + ephemeral KV logs + nightly snapshot EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED unless Medicore requests and justifies inclusion.
- Purge behavior: Automated purge tasks will remove backups at T+30 days. If Medicore invokes the rollback trigger (defined in exhibit B), backups may be retained until T+30 + 7 days post-rollback completion, after which purge runs immediately.
- Rollback trigger: defined criteria (failed data integrity checks across >1% of migrated keys, or corruption detected by checksum mismatch and infra sign-off). Rollback must be invoked via the Medicore incident process (legalops@medicore.com cc'd) and will be logged; all access during rollback will be token-audited.
- Subprocessors: Confirmed list attached. No additional subprocessors are used for the snapshot/backup flow beyond what's in subprocessor_matrix.csv.
- Cross-border transfer: If any part of the backup/restore flow transits non-EEA infra, Medicore must confirm transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent) prior to migration.

DocuSign: Kimberly has added the addendum to DocuSign. Sign here to accept: https://app.docusign.com/1234abcd (docusign_addendum_link.txt attached).

If these terms look OK, please sign the addendum and we'll schedule a short ops run-through on 22 Oct to validate the rollback path.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security & Trust — Redwood
[Attachment: redwood_temp-retention-proposal_20261020.pdf (application/pdf, 45KB)]
[Attachment: docusign_addendum_link.txt (text/plain, 1KB)]

From: Legal Ops (Medicore) <legalops@medicore.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: DPO - Medicore <dpo@medicore.com>, infra@medicore.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:18:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Proposed temporary-retention addendum and rollback trigger — MED-PROJ-21 (draft)

Thanks, Hannah — this is great and captures our needs. Two small edits:
1) We will accept 30 days as the default window.
2) Please add an explicit line that Redwood will provide a purge confirmation report (screenshot/log entry) within 48 hours of purge completion.

We've signed the DocuSign addendum — see attached signed_addendum_receipt.pdf and confirmation from our procurement team. We'll attend the ops run-through on 22 Oct 15:00 CET.

Sofia Ruiz
Legal Ops — Medicore Health
